{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "ULTRA MASTER PROMPT – Create a premium STATIC documentation landing page for a fictional entertainment archive called “The Velvet Marquee Guide”. It is NOT an app with accounts, not backend, no database, no API, no login, no payments. Everything is front-end only with mock/static content. Build it as a React static site using HTML/CSS/JS and GSAP animations. Theme: ART-DECO luxury cinema + theatre documentation portal, like a 1920s golden movie palace mixed with modern docs website. Needs to feel original, editorial, rich, and polished.

PROJECT GOAL
Design a landing page / documentation homepage for an entertainment knowledge system that teaches users how to explore classic film eras, theatre etiquette, stage lighting terms, soundtrack formats, award-season vocabulary, and festival guide basics. It should look like a serious documentation site but in a glamorous entertainment style. Imagine Stripe docs + Criterion Collection + old Hollywood art-deco hotel lobby.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS
- Static website only, renderable locally.
- No backend, no database, no real API, no auth, no user accounts.
- Use only mock data and hardcoded documentation sections.
- Do not use Three.js, WebGL, canvas games, physics, or game mechanics.
- Use GSAP for scroll animations / reveal animations / hero motion.
- Responsive desktop/tablet/mobile.
- Accessibility matters: semantic sections, readable contrast, focus states.

VISUAL STYLE
- Art-deco, premium, entertainment documentation.
- Colors: deep obsidian #09070d, velvet burgundy #4c1023, champagne gold #d7b46a, ivory #f8eed8, muted teal accent #1d6f73.
- Background should have subtle geometric deco patterns, gold divider lines, ornamental corner frames, radial glow like theatre spotlights.
- Typography: elegant serif display for headings, clean sans-serif for docs text. Can use CSS font stacks or imported Google Fonts if simple, but site must not depend on live data.
- Use glassy dark panels, gold borders, stepped geometry, marquee bulbs, ticket-stub cards, chapter numbers.
- Avoid generic SaaS blue-purple gradient look.

PAGE STRUCTURE
1. TOP NAVIGATION
- Left: logo mark “VM” inside art-deco badge + name “Velvet Marquee Guide”.
- Center nav links: Overview, Guides, Glossary, Playbooks, Timeline, FAQ.
- Right buttons: “Read the Docs” and “Download Static Kit” (fake CTA only, no actual download needed).
- Sticky nav with blur / gold line, shrink effect on scroll if possible.

2. HERO SECTION
Headline: “Documentation for the Golden Age of Entertainment Literacy”
Subheadline: “A static, beautifully indexed guide for film lovers, theatre hosts, festival volunteers, and soundtrack collectors.”
Add 2 CTA buttons: “Start with Overview” and “Browse Glossary”.
Hero visual: an art-deco documentation console with tabs, code-like doc snippets, a marquee sign, little gold animated lines, chapter cards floating subtly. Use GSAP entrance animation: title split/reveal, gold lines sweep in, cards stagger upward.
Include stats row:
- 48 curated guide pages
- 12 entertainment categories
- 1920s-inspired visual system
- 0 external services

3. DOCUMENTATION INDEX SECTION
Create complex docs layout with sidebar style mini navigation and cards.
Categories:
- Cinema Eras
- Theatre Operations
- Festival Basics
- Awards Vocabulary
- Soundtrack Formats
- Audience Etiquette
Each card should include short description, difficulty label, reading time, and small decorative icon using CSS/emoji/SVG inline (no image search required).
Add animated hover effects: gold border glow, small arrow slide.

4. FEATURED GUIDE SECTION
Title: “Featured Guide: How to Read a Premiere Night Program”
Create a two-column section:
Left: mock documentation article preview with headings, callout box, numbered steps.
Right: “Guide Anatomy” stacked cards: Credits, Runtime, Intermission, Sponsor Notes, Accessibility Cues.
Use GSAP scroll-trigger reveal and pin-like feeling if practical without overcomplicating.

5. INTERACTIVE STATIC GLOSSARY
No backend; create client-side filter tabs/buttons with static content only.
Tabs: Film, Stage, Music, Festivals, Awards.
When clicking a tab, show matching glossary cards from hardcoded data.
Examples terms:
- Overture
- Blocking
- Foley
- Palme-style Jury Note (fictional wording ok, do not mention real award brands if avoidable)
- House Lights
- Cue Sheet
Add micro animation when filtering, can use GSAP fade/stagger.

6. TIMELINE SECTION
A horizontal/vertical responsive timeline called “Entertainment Literacy Timeline”.
Items:
- 1910s Silent Hall Programs
- 1920s Deco Picture Palaces
- 1940s Studio Notes
- 1970s Festival Catalogues
- 1990s Home Video Guides
- 2020s Streaming Metadata
Each should have mock description and decorative year badge. Animate items on scroll.

7. PLAYBOOKS SECTION
Create cards for practical docs:
- “Hosting a Classic Film Night”
- “Building a Theatre Welcome Packet”
- “Explaining Credits to New Viewers”
- “Designing a Festival Day Plan”
Each card has checklist preview, tags, and CTA “Open playbook”. Static only.

8. ANIMATED MARQUEE STRIP
A horizontal looping marquee text using CSS or GSAP: “FILM NOTES • THEATRE GUIDES • SOUNDTRACK TERMS • FESTIVAL MAPS • AWARD SEASON VOCABULARY • STATIC DOCS •”
Must be elegant not annoying, pause on hover if possible.

9. COMPARISON / WHY THIS GUIDE
Create a table-like section comparing “Generic Wiki Notes” vs “Velvet Marquee Docs”.
Rows: Structure, Readability, Visual Cues, Offline Friendly, Beginner Pathways.
Use art-deco checkmarks and gold highlights.

10. FAQ SECTION
Accordion style static JS interaction. Questions:
- Is this connected to a real database?
- Can I customize the guide categories?
- Is the glossary content real?
- Does it work as a static site?
- Can GSAP animations be reduced for motion-sensitive users?
Answers should make clear it is static/mock and customizable.

11. FOOTER
Large art-deco footer with newsletter-looking box BUT no real signup. Input can be decorative only or disabled with text “Static demo only”. Links: Style System, Docs Map, Licensing Notes, Contact Placeholder. Add final line: “Built as a static entertainment documentation concept.”

ANIMATION REQUIREMENTS USING GSAP
- Hero title and cards stagger on load.
- ScrollTrigger reveals for sections.
- Timeline items animate in from alternating sides.
- Glossary filter transitions.
- Nav subtle shadow/line on scroll.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce or disable major animations.
- Keep animations smooth and classy, not childish.

RESPONSIVE REQUIREMENTS
- Desktop: rich multi-column layout, sticky mini sidebar in docs index if possible.
- Tablet: two-column where appropriate.
- Mobile: single column, nav collapses or wraps cleanly, cards readable, no horizontal overflow.

CONTENT TONE
Elegant but useful. It should read like a real documentation landing page, not lorem ipsum. Use polished microcopy and realistic sample docs text. Entertainment domain, but documentation scenario. No real celebrity names, no real brands necessary.

DELIVERABLE
A complete static React landing page with componentized sections, CSS styling, and GSAP animations. Mock content is enough. The final page should feel premium, complex, art-deco, and original.",

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
